title: query --kind --all
summary: Lists every symbol of one kind -- every unit, every class, every enum -- with no name, no doc clause and no row cap

help: drag-lint query              --name  <symbol-name>  [--db ...] [--json] [--case-sensitive] [--exact]
drag-lint query              --qname <qualified>    [--db ...] [--json] [--case-sensitive]
--name/--qname match CASE-INSENSITIVELY (Delphi identifiers are);
--case-sensitive restores byte-exact matching.
--name also accepts a QUALIFIED name (falls back to --qname on a dotted value).
--exact suppresses the fuzzy fallback, so 0 rows means "no such symbol".
JSON rows carry "match_kind": "exact" | "fuzzy" | "substring" (--name-like) -- reject "fuzzy" unless
you want suggestions; a fuzzy row does NOT carry the name you asked for.
--quiet suppresses the "(loaded defaults from ...)" stderr banner.
drag-lint query              --text "<phrase>" [--any-order|--substring] [--source pas|dfm|sql] [--kind <k>] [--limit N] [--db ...] [--json]
^ searches STRING LITERALS, DFM/SQL text AND COMMENT PROSE (// { } (* *) ///).
--kind literal|const|resourcestring|format|comment|doc|dfm-prop|sql-exception
narrows it; --kind literal reproduces the pre-comment behaviour exactly.
searches STRING LITERALS ONLY -- string constants, resourcestrings,
DFM captions, SQL exception messages. NOT source text: identifiers,
property assignments and type names are not in this corpus, so 0
matches for those is correct, not a missing index. COMMENTS: doc
comments ARE searchable -- `query find --doc-contains "<phrase>"`.
Only BODY-INLINE comments need grep. (INBOX 2.7; the old line here
sent people to grep for prose the index already had.)

pitfalls: a project DB IS the compile closure, so a hit is membership and a MISS is non-membership.

STRING LITERALS, DFM, SQL *and COMMENT PROSE* -- // { } (* *) and ///. Filter with --kind: literal|const|resourcestring|format|comment|doc|dfm-prop|sql-exception. --kind literal is what this returned before comments were indexed.
